offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: Event evt_000260, at provider-events partition 1 offset 113, carries an amount that is not a positive integer of cents. Both consumers reject it. payment-confirmer runs with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the event and moved on. ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:32:02 with BAD_EVENTS=retry, two seconds before the event arrived. Since then it has retried that one message without end, backing off up to 15 s between attempts, and has not moved past it. Its lag grows on all three partitions (72 each at 16:33:15), so the consumer stalls as a whole, not just partition 1. The money check therefore cannot settle the ledger up to its cutoff, which is the BooksBehindProvider symptom. Still open: what ledger-consumer's BAD_EVENTS setting was before this deploy (the deploy log is not visible to me in full), and why the provider event has a bad amount. Its origin is unclear, because payments-api runs CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents.

evidence.shows: The ledger consumer posts events while payment-confirmer dead-lettered one at 16:33. Consumer metrics only begin around 16:31, after the stack started.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:32:02 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
Ledger retries rise from 0 to 9 starting at 16:32:15. Ledger lag climbs on partitions 0, 1 and 2 (to 72 each), while confirmer lag stays at 0.
ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1@113, attempts 3 to 9, each with 'amount must be positive integer cents'. Backoff grows to 15 s.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1@113, at 16:32:04 for the same invalid amount.

The trace of evt_000260 shows webhook-receiver queued it to partition 1 at offset 113. The confirmer dead-lettered it. ledger-consumer has failed on it repeatedly for over 75 s with outcome will_retry.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 16:32:02 deploy, which presumably handled bad events without blocking (dead-lettering them), so it skips the poison message and drains its lag. Then do three things: examine evt_000260 in the dead letters and with the provider to see why its amount is invalid; book it by hand if it is a real movement of money; and rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and its lag grows briefly; no money is touched by the restart. If the prior setting dead-letters bad events, evt_000260 stays unbooked in the ledger until someone reviews and repairs it by hand. If the prior setting was also 'retry', the rollback will not unblock the consumer and the stall continues.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). The ledger handler is idempotent, so any reprocessed events are recognized as already processed.
